docai_lines.text: ABSTRACT
Introduction: Clinical governance can be defined as a framework or set of principles
and practices used to guide and oversee the delivery of clinical care. It aims to ensure
that patients receive safe, effective and high-quality care, in accordance with the best
available evidence and practice
Purpose: The purpose of this study was to investigate the perceptions of employees
regarding the climate of clinical governance in a General Hospital of Athens.
Materials and Methods: The research was conducted on a sample from the General
Hospital of Athens "Gennimatas," and the study sample consisted of 120 individuals
working in this hospital. The Greek version of the Clinical Governance Climate
Questionnaire (CGCQ) was used to investigate the climate of clinical governance in
the hospital. Descriptive and inferential statistical analyses were performed using the
SPSS v.26 statistical package.
Results: The findings show that 67% of employees have only a partial understanding
of clinical governance processes. 45% of employees with more than 10 years of
service showed higher levels of understanding compared to 25% of employees with
less than 5 years of service. The correlation between experience and understanding is
statistically significant (r = 0.82, p < 0.05). Physicians reported a better understanding
of policies at 70% compared to 50% of nurses, with the correlation also being
statistically significant (Spearman rho = 0.60, p < 0.05). Additionally, a significant
negative correlation was found between the age of employees and their willingness to
change clinical practices (r = -0.76, p < 0.01). The relationship between education
level and understanding of governance processes was also significant (r = 0.68, p <
0.05). Finally, employees who actively participate in decision-making processes
reported higher levels of job satisfaction (r = 0.85, p < 0.001).
Conclusions: The results indicate that there is partial understanding of governance
processes by the majority of employees, highlighting the need for improved
educational initiatives and clearer communication of policies. The difference in
understanding between various professional groups, with physicians having a higher
understanding compared to nurses, indicates the need for uniform educational policies
